headline: 30 hours: CUET VC freed after blockade by students
summary: District Commissioner and SP rescue newly appointed VC Prof. Sheikh Shariful Alam from the administrative building after a nearly 30-hour confinement.
details: Newly appointed Vice Chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, was freed after being confined to the administrative building for nearly 30 hours.
The rescue operation was led by District Commissioner (DC) Mohammad Zahidul Islam Mia and Superintendent of Police (SP) Md. Masud Alam, who negotiated with protesting students on Tuesday evening.
Students allowed the VC to leave on the condition that he would not return to the campus. The VC and other confined individuals were subsequently taken away in an ambulance for medical treatment.
The protests began after Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem was removed and replaced by Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam on September 21.
Students, teachers, and staff have been observing a 'complete shutdown' and work abstention since September 22 to demand the reinstatement of the former VC.
The situation escalated when the VC entered his office by breaking locks on the administrative building, which students had previously locked to prevent his entry.
caption:
Confined for nearly 30 hours, the CUET VC was finally freed after the DC and SP intervened.

Newly appointed Vice Chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, was freed after being confined to the administrative building for nearly 30 hours.

The rescue operation was led by District Commissioner (DC) Mohammad Zahidul Islam Mia and Superintendent of Police (SP) Md. Masud Alam, who negotiated with protesting students on Tuesday evening.

Students allowed the VC to leave on the condition that he would not return to the campus. The VC and other confined individuals were subsequently taken away in an ambulance for medical treatment.

The protests began after Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem was removed and replaced by Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam on September 21.

Students, teachers, and staff have been observing a 'complete shutdown' and work abstention since September 22 to demand the reinstatement of the former VC.

The situation escalated when the VC entered his office by breaking locks on the administrative building, which students had previously locked to prevent his entry.

headline_marked: Litton Das [[sets world record]] on 32nd birthday
headline: Litton Das sets world record on 32nd birthday
summary: The wicketkeeper-batter became the first in Test history to record nine dismissals while scoring a century and a fifty in the same match.
details: Litton Das achieved a historic milestone on his 32nd birthday during Bangladesh's one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi.
He became the first cricketer in Test history to record nine dismissals as a wicketkeeper while scoring both a century and a half-century in the same match.
Litton broke the previous record of eight dismissals, which was set by South Africa's Denis Lindsay in 1966.
With the bat, Litton was outstanding, scoring 53 in the first innings and 102 in the second innings.
Behind the stumps, he recorded nine dismissals in total, including a stunning one-handed diving catch to dismiss Ikram Alikhil.
Litton had already set a Bangladesh national record on the previous day by recording eight dismissals in a single Test.
He is now just two dismissals away from joining the record for the most dismissals in a single Test match, currently held by Jack Russell, AB de Villiers, and Rishabh Pant with 11.
caption:
A birthday to remember! Litton Das just made Test history by setting a new world record.

Litton Das achieved a historic milestone on his 32nd birthday during Bangladesh's one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi.

He became the first cricketer in Test history to record nine dismissals as a wicketkeeper while scoring both a century and a half-century in the same match.

Litton broke the previous record of eight dismissals, which was set by South Africa's Denis Lindsay in 1966.

With the bat, Litton was outstanding, scoring 53 in the first innings and 102 in the second innings.

Behind the stumps, he recorded nine dismissals in total, including a stunning one-handed diving catch to dismiss Ikram Alikhil.

Litton had already set a Bangladesh national record on the previous day by recording eight dismissals in a single Test.

He is now just two dismissals away from joining the record for the most dismissals in a single Test match, currently held by Jack Russell, AB de Villiers, and Rishabh Pant with 11.
